_about: written judgement about what each model is for. SOURCE, not derived: analyze-usecase
carries it into data/usecase.json beside the numbers, and never overwrites it.
the numbers lead. every `evidence` entry names a facet and the percentile the model
holds on it WITHIN this registry -- p79 means it beat 79% of the registry models that
carry the same facet, not 79% of every model in the world. `claim` marks a number the
model published about itself, which analyze-self-report measures as running about +0.9
high, and which is the weakest evidence here.
confidence is about the EVIDENCE, not the model: high means several independent
third-party sources agree, medium means one source or a thin sample, low means nobody
has measured it and this is the card plus whatever the forums said.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B.one_liner: the strongest open-weights model this corpus measures, and the one nothing here can load.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.one_liner: the strongest dense model in the registry on measured axes, and the current default answer for a single 27b that has to do everything.
Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.notes: gbench has not played it yet, so its evidence is aa plus its own card plus 175 reddit mentions at 91% approval. the template defaults thinking to xhigh, which costs 15k-52k thinking tokens in reported traces against qwen3.6's 3k. it is also the value pick: the top score out of the smallest file of anything near it, which leaves most of a 128gb box free for context or a second model. one reproducible benchmark on this exact silicon reports UD-Q5_K_XL at 16.68 t/s against Q8_0's 12.74, with MTP at 4 draft tokens under vulkan -- one reporter on one box, so a reason to test the lower quant rather than a recommendation to run it.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.one_liner: the qwen4 architecture preview, and the highest-measured model here that still fits the box -- bought with a 51b n-gram table that is most of what makes it awkward to serve.
Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.notes: artificial analysis scored it three days after release, and it leads qwen3.8-27b on every axis the two share: II 55.8 against 52.0, coding 73.1 against 68.1, agentic 56.4 against 50.9, terminal-bench 86.1 against 79.8. the exception is the one to know about -- non-hallucination p66 against qwen3.8-27b's p93, so it answers where the 27b declines. what the forums discuss is none of that. 75 huggingface discussion posts, almost all about speed and memory: 11 t/s reported without MTP, and no mainline gguf has an MTP head because llama.cpp's converter drops it and PR 27836 is still open. 41% of the file is the n-gram table, which is what both the '4x slower than it should be' and the 'keep the n-gram table on nvme' threads are about, and it is also why the quant ladder bottoms out at 67.6gib -- its 160-column rows take only block-32 types. AtomicChat is the one publisher that shards the table separately, so 38 of their 93 gb page from ssd rather than staying resident.
evidence: hf-discussions 75 mentions p97, reddit 62 mentions at 100% approval on two scored posts

deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.one_liner: the registry's strongest all-rounder: top decile on science, coding, long context and physics at once, and the most discussed model after qwen3.6.
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.notes: at UD-IQ3_XXS it is 97gib, so on a 128gb box it fits with a drafter and little else. best go play measured here at 82%. v4's compressed sparse attention makes the kv cache far cheaper than a generic reserve assumes -- deepseek reports the 1m setting costing 27% of what the naive form would -- which is what leaves room for the 10.2gib dspark drafter beside it. two complaints from people actually running it: it ignores rules files and skill definitions, which the thread attributes to deepseek shipping no official jinja template and each quant publisher writing their own, so pin a known-good template rather than trusting the gguf default; and where the fitting quant is too tight, the community's answer for this class of box is Rednalreden's dwarfstar, a single 80.8gib file that keeps Q8 attention projections, shared experts and output layer while dropping the routed experts to IQ2_XXS.

deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.one_liner: a 552b multimodal moe whose whole argument is the kv cache -- 890 bytes a token, a quarter of v4 flash -- and which nothing on this roster can currently run.
use_for: tracking what the roster cannot currently load
agentic coding, on its own claims
avoid_for: anything where the claim needs to be independently checked
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.notes: released 2026-09-10, so no third-party suite has scored it and every id resolves to nothing; the card is all there is. what it claims is worth watching for this roster specifically: the global kv cache is 890 bytes per token against v4 flash's ~3.5kib, which is the number that decides whether a 1m context is affordable rather than nominal, and only 8b of 552b is active in prefill. the checkpoint also takes images, which v4 flash did not. the practical position is the opposite of the claims. one complete gguf exists -- apetersson's 157gib mixed-q2, uncalibrated, missing the engram tables, the dspark blocks and the vision tensors -- and its own publisher records that no runtime has executed it end to end: llama.cpp's converter PR is a draft and converter-only, vllm has no deepseek tensor map in its gguf plugin, and the sglang path needs a four-rule mapper patch plus a 180-288gb card with the engram tables host-resident. the conventional k-quant ladder everyone is actually waiting for is vcruz305's, and it is 37% uploaded -- 383 of 1046 tensors over 3 of 7 shards -- so the 95.75 gib beside it is a third of a pack rather than a rung that fits. treat the card facets here with more than the usual suspicion: the extractor read the BASE model table, so `card.gpqa` is the 53.1 of supergpqa rather than the 90.9 the instruct model claims on gpqa diamond.
evidence: no third-party suite scores it: aa, gbench, lmarena, swerebench and epoch are all empty
the only complete gguf is 157.33 gib at 2.45 read bits per weight, and no runtime has loaded it

tencent/Hy3.one_liner: top-decile on reasoning and the best-rated model here by human preference, with a gbench sample too thin to quote.
tencent/Hy3.notes: gbench has played it 7 games over 25 matches, which is why its gscore is marked thin rather than used. 49 reddit mentions at 93% approval is the best reception in the registry. the ranking and the people running it disagree, and the disagreement is worth more than either. a handful on 128gb machines rate it first for coding -- "significantly better coder than deepseek-v4-flash, keep using deepseek-v4-flash only if speed is the primary concern" -- against a similar number who found it slow. both can be true: AA measures the unquantized model, the retention curve is transferred from another architecture, and 21b active is more compute per token than anything else that fits. what people report costing them is context and speed rather than quality, roughly 190k against deepseek's 1m, with throughput that drops off brutally as context grows.

thinkingmachines/Inkling.one_liner: the flagship the small is small relative to, and it is ahead on only eleven of the twenty-nine facets they share.

thinkingmachines/Inkling.notes: the reason to carry it was to find out what inkling small gives up, and the answer is: knowledge and human preference, not reasoning. it wins simpleqa by 43 points, lmarena by 47 and long-context recall by 17, and it LOSES proofbench by 31 and aime by 21 to a model a fraction of its size. omniscience p93 with omniscience_index p88 says it knows more and does not pay for it in hallucination, which is the clearest case for the extra weight. nothing about that is runnable here -- bf16 is 1.76 tib and the smallest rung is 252 gib, so this is a reference point like kimi k3.
evidence: epoch.simpleqa_verified p57, against inkling small p14
lmarena.rating p71, against inkling small p24
epoch.proofbench p0, against inkling small p31

yuxinlu1/gemma-4-12B-agentic-fable5-comp.one_liner: the same 12b continued into tool use, carrying one agentic number that its own author ran.

avoid_for: customer-service style agents -- the card puts the base model AHEAD of it on tau2 retail
